record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.context_brief: Continuous harmonic maps from B^3 to S^2
record.original_question: Let Ω = B^3 be the unit ball in R^3 and let g: ∂Ω ≃ S^2 → S^2 be a smooth boundary map of degree zero. Does there exist a continuous harmonic map u: Ω → S^2 satisfying -Δu_i = u_i|∇u|^2 for i=1,2,3 in Ω, |u(x)|=1 in Ω, and u=g on ∂Ω?

evidence.quote: Since we will be concerned with the existence of continuous harmonic maps satisfying (4.3) we assume throughout this section that (4.6) deg g = 0. Here is a long-standing open problem originally posed by R. Schoen in the mid-1980’s: Open Problem 4.1 ([HaLi], [Ha], [Br5, Open Problem 3]). Assume that (4.6) holds. Does there exist a continuous harmonic map satisfying (4.1)-(4.3)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = B^3 = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^3 : |x| < 1\}$ be the open unit ball, with boundary $\partial \Omega = S^2$. Let $g : S^2 \to S^2$ be a smooth map of topological degree zero. A map $u : \Omega \to S^2 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$, $u = (u_1, u_2, u_3)$, is called a harmonic map if $|u(x)| = 1$ for all $x \in \Omega$ and the harmonic map equation
$$-\Delta u_i = u_i\, |\nabla u|^2 \qquad (i = 1, 2, 3)$$
holds in $\Omega$ (in the sense of distributions).

Question: Does there exist a continuous map $u : \overline{\Omega} \to S^2$ which is harmonic in $\Omega$ (in the above sense) and which satisfies the Dirichlet boundary condition $u = g$ on $\partial \Omega$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is the long-standing open problem of R. Schoen (mid-1980s) on existence of a continuous harmonic map from $B^3$ to $S^2$ with prescribed degree-zero smooth boundary data. It is referenced as an open problem in surveys by Hardt–Lin, Hardt, and Brezis, and no resolution is recorded in the literature retrieved. Status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Analytic Aspects of the Harmonic Map Problem (Schoen)
status_evidence.snippet: Schoen's article posing analytic problems on harmonic maps including existence and regularity for the Dirichlet problem into S^2.
status_evidence.claim: The problem originates with Schoen's discussion of analytic aspects of harmonic maps.

status_evidence.title: Some new harmonic maps from B^3 to S^2
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of harmonic maps from B^3 to S^2 with various boundary data, related to Schoen's existence/regularity questions.
status_evidence.claim: Related constructions exist but do not settle the degree-zero continuous existence question.
